summary.tpReason: MailGuard recorded the exact message as inbound Phish (92 confidence) after Sandbox analysis; the macro-enabled attachment and SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures support a genuine hostile lure. The same sender infrastructure delivered a second malicious message to mirage shortly before confirmed identity and AWS abuse from the shared source IP.
summary.fpReason: The admin-targeted message itself was quarantined, and no endpoint, Office activity, or Entra sign-in evidence shows that admin opened it or was compromised. The small residual uncertainty is limited to whether all activity from the shared sender/IP is one causally linked campaign.
summary.whatHappened: At 2026-08-19 06:54:26Z, noreply@malicious-infra.xyz (198.51.100.42) sent admin@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com the subject “RE: Meeting Notes — Please Review Attachment” with meeting-notes.docm (SHA-256 a1b2…a1b2). MailGuard Sandbox classified it Phish (92) and quarantined it; all SPF, DKIM and DMARC checks failed. The same IP/domain sent an allowed phishing email with report.exe to mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com at 06:50:37Z. At 07:36Z, mirage authenticated to Okta from 198.51.100.42/RU and then granted super-admin, created “Backdoor API Token,” reset/deactivated MFA factors, and enrolled attacker TOTP. From 07:52Z, the same IP successfully used AWS user mirage: it created/admin-enabled backdoor-svc, exposed a security group, started five p3.16xlarge instances, retrieved finance/HR/API-key S3 objects, and stopped/deleted CloudTrail. backdoor-svc subsequently logged in from 198.51.100.42 and 203.0.113.77.
keyEvidence: MailGuard365_Threats_CL: exact admin message at 06:54:26Z was inbound, Action=Quarantine, ThreatVerdict=Phish, ThreatConfidence=92, ScanEngine=MailGuard Sandbox; meeting-notes.docm was a .docm and SPF/DKIM/DMARC all failed.
MailGuard365_Threats_CL found two messages from malicious-infra.xyz / 198.51.100.42: the admin mail was quarantined, but a report.exe lure was allowed to mirage at 06:50:37Z.

OktaV2_CL: mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com logged in successfully from 198.51.100.42 (Moscow, RU) at 07:36Z, then successfully granted super admin, created Backdoor API Token, modified MFA factors, and enrolled attacker-controlled TOTP.
AWSCloudTrail: mirage successfully created backdoor-svc, created an active access key, attached AdministratorAccess, and created a console profile; no AWS errors were recorded for those requests.

AWSCloudTrail: the same session retrieved corp-data-prod finance/2026-budget-final.xlsx, hr/employee-records-full.csv, and secrets/api-keys-production.json; it also stopped and deleted management-events-trail, exposed 0.0.0.0/0 ingress, and launched five p3.16xlarge instances.
AWSCloudTrail: backdoor-svc subsequently completed console logins from 198.51.100.42 and 203.0.113.77, demonstrating persistence beyond the mirage session.
researchDone: Queried MailGuard365_Threats_CL and SEG_MailGuard_CL for the exact message ID, sender/domain, recipient, and 18–20 Aug window. MailGuard supplied the two-message campaign; SEG had no matching duplicate records.
Queried SecurityAlert for related sender/IP, recipient, URL, and hash indicators through 21 Aug. This exposed correlated Okta/AWS alerts involving mirage and the shared IP.
Queried OktaV2_CL for mirage and 198.51.100.42, confirming successful authentication and privileged/MFA/API-token actions with timestamps and targets.
Queried AWSCloudTrail for mirage, backdoor-svc, and 198.51.100.42, confirming successful persistence, resource changes, S3 object access, and logging disruption.
Checked admin sign_in_adelete_CL and OfficeActivity_CL for 18 Aug 06:54Z–20 Aug 12:00Z: no admin sign-ins, mailbox activity, attachment access, or rule changes were returned.

Checked mirage OfficeActivity_CL and CrowdStrikeDetections for post-delivery corroboration; neither returned activity/detections. CrowdStrikeHosts only associates mirage with win11a, last seen 2026-08-15, so endpoint execution is not established.
